posts.caption: New thing on Wednesdays: Bench Notes. One small habit from the bench, every week. First one: before you call a receiver noisy, work every pot and switch 20 times with a shot of DeoxIT D5. Half the crackle you hear at estate sales is just 40 years of dust. Bench Notes 01

Bench Notes 02. Nothing from an estate sale gets plugged straight into the wall here. It goes through the dim-bulb tester first: a 60 W bulb in series with the mains. Bulb flares and settles, good. Bulb stays bright, something is shorted and you just saved a transformer.
Left: the original 8 V incandescent. Right: the cold-white LED someone dropped in. Which dial would you rather read at night? We go warm every time. Bench Notes 03 #vintageaudio #hifi

Measuring a belt the honest way: string around the pulley and platter path, mark it, subtract a little for stretch. Guessing from a part number is how you end up with a platter that runs fast. (Bench Notes 04)
After a recap, the meter goes on the speaker terminals before the speakers do. DC offset should sit in the low millivolts. If it doesn't, the speakers stay in the box. 05
Walnut veneer, cleaned the slow way. Naphtha on a cloth, test spot inside the back panel, wipe with the grain, oil last and thin. What's the worst finish you've rescued? Bench Notes 06
Press gently. If it crumbles, it's a refoam. 🔊 #BenchNotes
How a receiver leaves the shop: knobs off and bagged, inner box, two inches of foam on every side, outer box. Every one gets photographed before the tape goes on. Bench Notes 08
Dial cord rule: photograph the string path before you loosen anything. Every manufacturer routed it differently and none of them drew you a map. Back from a week off, Bench Notes 09.
Cassette deck running slow? Look at the pinch roller. Shiny and hard means it slips. New belts plus a roller cleaned or replaced, and most decks come right back. 10
30x loupe. Takes ten seconds and tells you if that stylus is going to chew your records. Bench Notes 11
We don't shotgun every capacitor on a board. Power supply first, then whatever the measurements point to. Fewer new parts, fewer new problems. Bench Notes 12 #recap #vintagehifi #detroit
Turntable hum, in order: ground wire to the amp's GND post, then swap the cables, then try a different outlet. Nine times out of ten it's the first one. Bench Notes 13
Thirteen Wednesdays of Bench Notes in 60 seconds. Which one should get a longer video? 🎥
That glow is the reason half of you buy vintage. When a meter lamp goes, we match the color, not just the voltage. Bench Notes 15
Old grease in a turntable changer doesn't lubricate anymore, it glues. Clean it all out, then relube sparingly. More is not better. 16
First power-up after service goes into a dummy load, never your speakers. 8 ohms of resistors that don't care if something goes wrong. Bench Notes 17
Fuses. Same rating, same type, slow-blow stays slow-blow. A bigger fuse doesn't fix anything, it just moves the failure somewhere more expensive. Bench Notes 19
Contact cleaner and lubricant are not the same can. One goes in switches and pots. The other goes on bearings and nowhere near a switch. Bench Notes 20
One channel dead? Before you open it up, check the tape monitor button and the speaker selector. You'd be amazed how many 'broken' receivers we've fixed with a finger. 21
Cold joint on the left, reflowed on the right. Dull and ringed means it's time for fresh solder. Bench Notes 22

Speed check, no tools: print a strobe disc, set it on the platter, light it with a bulb that flickers at mains frequency (most cheap LEDs do). Bars standing still at 33 1/3 means you're on speed. Bench Notes 23

Bench Notes #24. Cold-weather rule: gear that rode home in a cold van sits on the bench until it's room temperature. Power it on cold and the condensation inside does the rest. Give it a few hours. Season's turning, so this one matters again.

CAW-1129 Pioneer SX-780, back from the bench. Power supply recapped, new dial lamps, every function to spec. Very Good by our grading guide: light scuffs on the cover, faceplate and glass clean. $425, pick-up in Detroit or UPS Ground. DM us.
Coming soon. CAW-1138, Technics SL-1200MK2 in silver, just off the bench and locked on the strobe at both speeds.
Same bench, new colours. VU Amber, after the meter glow on a warmed-up receiver. The shop site has moved too: corktownaudio.com, link in bio.

KLH Model Six, the pair. Teak cabinets cleaned and oiled, grilles re-tensioned, woofers and tweeters swept clean on the bench. Very Good per our grading guide. CAW-1072 goes on Marketplace Thursday, DMs open.

Power supply recapped, 30 W/ch at under 0.1% THD on both channels, every lamp lit. Graded Excellent by our written guide, with one ~2 cm hairline on the case top, rear left. Swipe for the raking-light shot.

$575 + shipping. DM us or find it on Marketplace.

#marantz #vintagehifi #detroithifi

Five grades, written down, same for every piece: Mint, Excellent, Very Good, Good, For Parts. Excellent means light hairlines you'd only catch up close or under a raking light. No chips, dents, cracks or veneer damage, and everything works to spec. Wear you can see at arm's length makes it Very Good at best, and the listing says so.

Best thing to come into the workshop this month isn't a receiver. Paper cones, veneer and a humid Detroit June don't get along, so the dehumidifier runs all summer now. Anyone else fighting that basement smell?
Shipping and pick-ups pause for the holiday weekend, Fri 7/3 through Mon 7/6, and replies may be slow. Back at the bench Tuesday. Enjoy the long weekend 🎆
Restocked. Double-wall cartons, fresh foam, a few miles of tape. Every receiver leaves here double-boxed.
The van came home full from Boston-Edison. Nothing in it gets listed until it's been through the bench. #vintagehifi #detroit #estatesale

CAW-1090, Marantz 2220B. Graded Excellent. There's one hairline, and you'll need to get within a few inches to find it. Otherwise it's what you'd hope for from a 2220B: that blue dial, smooth tuning and a sound you can listen to all evening.

Honest one: this Pioneer PL-12D (CAW-1115) looks clean, but on the bench the motor won't hold speed, so it's graded For Parts. If you've got another PL-12D that needs a donor, or you like a motor project, this is your deck.
